_about: Names for Karateka's routines and globals, with the evidence for each.
This file exists because `recovered/karateka.asm` is gitignored and must
stay so -- a byte-identical reconstruction is the game. What can be kept
is the *reading*: addresses, names, and why. Run tools/annotate.py to
apply these to a freshly generated listing and get source that still
reassembles to the original, byte for byte.
Addresses are image offsets. Add 0x200 for a file offset. Globals are
offsets from DS, which the entry stub sets to image + 0x6CA0.
`why` is not decoration. A name with no evidence behind it is a guess
that will be believed by the next reader, and this project has already
published three of those and had to withdraw them.

0x0002: sets DS=0x6CA, SS=0x155C, SP=0x80, enables interrupts (cli...sti) -- the classic Lattice C MZ-entry prologue, lines 363-369
calls INT 21h AH=0x30 (get DOS version) as literally the first service request the program makes, line 370-371
0x00220: DX=0xc7, AH=9, INT 21h -- DOS print-string of the message at DS:0xC7, lines 633-635
AH=0x4C01, INT 21h after a DOS-version gate -- terminates with exit code 1, lines 637-639
0x0023C: cmp byte[dos_version],2 / jl L_0024C gates everything that follows on the DOS version, lines 645-646
falls through to AH=0x4C / INT 21h only when the version check passes, lines 647-649 -- an exit, not a mere query, so the name covers a version-gated exit path
0x0255: calls choose_adapter, load_input_table and load_player_library in sequence before anything else runs, lines 672/681/707 -- a one-time startup phase

calls main exactly once (line 724) between the startup phase and the L_00316 loop -- named 'startup' because it is what hands off to main, even though the function also goes on to host the game loop afterward (see October's note, not wrong, just a second phase of the same function)
0x03C7: loads ALLVAL (compile_script), fuji.bcg (load_backdrop) and scene 0 (load_scene) before any card is shown, lines 827-839 -- more than a title loop alone

loops through show_frame/card_author/card_port_credit/card_sprite/card_opening, each falling to play_attract on timeout, lines 845-875 -- the part October's 'title_loop' correctly captures, kept as a second observation rather than renaming
0x0569: cmp word[player_down],1 then cmp word[player_pose],0x43 -- two of the three level-end conditions, testing player state, not keyboard hardware
cmp word[player_x],word[level_right] -- the third level-end condition, comparing the player's position against the level's right wall global
0x05AD: calls show_castle, then load_backdrop on fuji.bcg -- the two-backdrop sequence that gives the routine its name
calls load_scene(0) followed by compile_script and advance_script -- loads and runs the attract-mode script after the images are shown
0x0608: AH=0 before INT 10h -- the BIOS 'set video mode' function number, not merely 'a video interrupt'
AL comes straight from word[bp+4], the caller's single argument -- a thin one-argument wrapper, matching the name
0x0614: AH=2 before INT 10h -- BIOS set-cursor-position, not a generic video call
DL and DH are built from the routine's two stack arguments (bp+4, bp+6) -- a two-argument (row, col) wrapper
0x0629: rand() * (n+1), high word taken -- uniform 0..n with no divide
0x0640: and al,3 / shl al,1 / mov[shift_in_byte],al -- a 2-bit sub-byte shift amount is computed and stored, unique to the shifted variant
mov byte[shape_run_count],0 / mov byte[mask_run_count],0 at entry -- resets both RLE run counters before decoding a fresh sprite, shared setup with draw_sprite proper
0x083C: mov byte[shape_run_count],0 / mov byte[mask_run_count],0 at entry -- same RLE-stream setup as draw_sprite_shifted, confirming it is the sibling blit routine
jmp draw_sprite_clip when the destination column goes negative -- delegates clipping instead of handling the sub-byte shift itself
0x0093F: one row of the sprite; the column loop at 0x00A6F jumps back to it
0x00957: the clipped entry: draw_sprite jumps here when the sprite crosses an edge and the row loop has to start part-way in
0x00A1E: the draw proper, once the caller has decided there is something to draw. blit_column tail-jumps in
0x00A69: pop bp and return -- the shared exit both halves reach
0x00A6B: reloads the sprite cursor from 0x421E before the next column
0x00A9F: advances to the next column and re-enters the row loop
0x0AE7: one byte per scanline, add di 0x50
0x00B1E: reloads SI from the sprite cursor and walks the mask table at 0x443C
0x00B4E: lea di,[screen_buffer] -- targets the named off-screen frame buffer specifically, not any other region
mov cx,0x1f40 (8000) / rep stosw with AX=0 -- a full zero-fill of exactly the buffer's word count
0x00B5E: cmp byte[si+sprite_data],0x7b (lines 1677-1678) -- recognises the 0x7B escape byte that starts a run
on escape, reads count then value, in that order (lines 1679-1682), both from the shape stream -- the opposite byte order October's evidence describes
0x0B95: run-length decoder, called once per output byte
0x00BC9: mov word[draw_layer],3 at function start, then add word[draw_layer],4 each iteration -- a counted walk over fixed-stride table entries
terminates on byte==0xFF and dispatches draw_sprite_shifted or draw_sprite per layer
0x00C52: lea si,[sprite_table_b] / lea di,[screen_r80c0] / rep movsw -- the sprite-table copy that gives the routine its name
lea di,[screen_r154c0] ... rep stosw twice with AX and NOT AX (lines ~1803-1811) -- draws the striped band beneath the sprites, the 'whole picture' August's evidence describes
0x00D68: mov ax,0xb800 / mov es,ax -- targets the CGA display segment specifically
a 200-row (cmp bx,0x190) loop of rep movsw -- copies the entire off-screen frame, not a partial band
0x00D89: two candidate bands (screen_r32c0, screen_r116c0) are chosen between by comparing draw_enable against redraw_all
dl (the row count) and bx (the row-offset base) are both adjusted together for the second band -- one coherent 'which band' decision, not two independent ones
0x00DD0: the band at screen_r114c0, chosen by scene
0x00DEF: three passes, each isolating a different 2-bit field (0xc0, 0x30, 0xc) of the same source byte -- a progressive reveal, not a single copy
call spin_1000 between passes -- a deliberate pause, consistent with a fade rather than an instant blit
0x00EE8: a thousand turns of an empty loop; the only delay the drawing code has
0x00EEE: one sprite from sprite_table_a at screen_r70c0, cleared and blitted around it
0x00F27: clear, draw, blit, wait -- the four calls every title card makes, with draw_ready deciding whether there is anything to draw
0x0FBB: loads castle.bcg and runs it through the script player
0x1027: strcpy/strcat build a filename from the caller's index
0x1277: call fopen then a fgets/compile_line loop until fgets returns 0 -- a text-file compile loop, not a stage driver
call file_flush_if_dirty then stores the result in compile_count -- the compiled byte count the name's 'byte code out' refers to
0x12EB: a 14-iteration (cmp ax,0xe) strncmp loop against a command-name table -- matching one of the fourteen known script commands
jmp compile_dispatch with the matched index in AX -- hands off to the arm that emits bytecode for that command, not to any draw or sound routine
0x1364: arm 0 of the compiler's jump table at 0x163E
0x162D: arm 13; emits 0xFF, the only opcode that is not 2*index
0x0165A: bounds the command against 0x0E and jumps through animation_dispatch
0x01668: drops the 0x12-byte frame and returns; every compile_ routine ends here
0x166D: walks compiled byte code; polls for a key with AH=06
0x0169C: `mov sp, bp` then a pushed return to 0x02B8: the long jump out of a failed load
0x016A3: AH=6, DL=0xFF -- DOS direct console I/O's 'check if a key is waiting' form
on Esc (0x1b) or Ctrl-Break (0x11... wait this project's own cmp al,0x11), resets video mode (INT 10h AH implied 3) then exits via INT 21h AH=0x4C -- the literal 'quit' this function checks for
0x01718: compares a script command's name against script_limits, character by character
0x01734: steps script_cursor, honours wipe_pending, and skips the demo-only commands when demo_mode is clear
0x017FB: pops one level of script_depth back into script_cursor
0x0186C: redraw_all to 0xFFFF, the draw_layer bounds to 3 and 0, palette_byte cleared, and script_cursor stepped
0x018BF: computes target=now+AX immediately after the first INT 1Ah, not just reading the clock once
the loop condition is cmp dx,word[script_arg] -- a comparison against that stored target, confirming it waits for a duration, not a single tick change
0x018D5: AX/2 rounds of a two-tick wait, abandoned as soon as read_intent reports a key
0x018EF: the only thing the function does besides the INT1Ah call is store DX into script_pc -- a pure mark/record operation
script_pc is the same global wait_3_ticks (0x18F8) later subtracts from -- the two functions pair as mark-then-wait
0x018F8: cmp dx,3 / jb wait_3_ticks -- the literal '3' in the name is the loop's own threshold
mov word[script_pc],ax after the loop exits -- re-marks the tick for the next call, consistent with repeated use in a script-timing loop
0x190B: compile a named script and run it
0x1976: walks a compiled library recording each block's offset; 42 of them, frames 17 bytes
0x0197E: walks a move library building 0x2A index entries, skipping the two-byte 0x18 records and stopping at 0xFF
0x19A2: the same for the library at 0xCE3E
0x19EE: builds n section tables from a scenery script; n is 1 or 6
0x1AC2: scene 0..3 -> bal00..bal03 through the pointer table at DS:0x021C
0x1B27: reads a per-level table (si=level*2) into player_x, level_left, level_right -- sets the walls, as named
calls reset_guard exactly once, which is where the starting health and pose actually get set (see 0x1C58) -- 'init_fight' correctly describes a one-time setup, not a per-frame engine
0x1C58: sets guard_x from a per-level table and then conditionally subtracts 0x140 (one screen width) for level>1 -- position reset
sets guard_pose and guard_health to fixed starting values (0x41/1, 0xd) in the same function -- pose and health reset, together with position
0x1D07: called from at least 7 sites in the pose switch (lines 4141-4271), not zero
calls read_intent, poll_intent, handle_key and pose_action in sequence -- the input-handling chain, not a high-score screen
0x1D8A: calls read_intent(0) once and reports whether anything was pressed
0x1DD5: folds A-Z to lower case and compares -- the letter commands
0x1F4E: switches on player_pose through the table at 0x200A
0x214B: poses 1 and 8; no input becomes move 0, anything else passes through
0x2161: poses 2-4; no input becomes 41, anything else is offset by +34
0x21DB: poses 10 and 11; intent 12 in pose 10 stays 12
0x2211: pose 15; `xor ax, ax` and return -- this pose accepts no input at all
0x2218: poses 65 and 66; no input becomes move 19
0x228B: sparse (pose, arm) dispatch, seventeen cases, table at 0x2247
0x22A4: rep movsb from [bp+6] to [bp+4], count = [bp+8]-[bp+6]; 164 calls per run from fight_frame
0x22BC: one frame for both fighters: advance, or choose and start a move
0x022E1: one turn of the fight: both cursors, both positions, the phase, and whichever of player_choose_move, guard_choose_move or demo_choose_move applies
0x2324: advance or restart the player's move
0x02461: one comparison on the phase decides whether the player or the guard moves next
0x025CD: the guard's half, entered directly when the phase says so
0x2605: the AI: its pose, the player's pose, the distance
0x2A0A: push bp / mov bp, sp / pop bp / ret -- five bytes that do nothing. Nothing calls it, so comrec emits it as five `db` bytes with no label and this name is documentation only
0x2A49: plays the attract sequence; computes a distance a keyboard reader would not want
0x2B94: random(255) under 0x32, and only inside 0x4B -- a one-in-five roll
0x2BDD: calls hit_test for each fighter and applies the damage
0x2F2D: advances section_index and the right wall
0x2F98: drops guard_health on a scripted beat rather than a hit
0x0301C: directly compares and zeroes player_health/guard_health based on player_down, defeat_flag, patience_a and patience_b -- all named globals from the fight-state table this project already tracks
subtracts defeat_pending from player_health and hit_flash from guard_health to decide whether to draw a defeat word -- the comparison and its consequence in one function
0x03162: seven words of zero at stride 0x50
0x0316F: seven words from SI at the same stride
0x31AA: reads and rewrites story_event through several cmp/mov pairs -- a state machine over one variable, i.e. a 'step'
cmp word[story_gate_c],0 / cmp word[guard_present],0 / cmp word[player_pose],0x1c gate a card_the_end call -- advancing the story only under specific conditions, not every frame unconditionally
0x3A2D: sets the walls and the section index
0x3A8A: copies section [0xC3A6] out of the three tables
0x3AD0: re-reads section_index into the three live pointers
0x3B19: pose 31, and random(2)*12 for an aggression of 0, 12 or 24
0x3B5C: knock back 4 px and take a point; the scripted kind, not the fight kind
0x3BAE: takes a sound-id argument (bp+4) and early-outs on 0, dispatching through a jump table by id (line ~6971) -- a routine that plays one of several sounds, not a bare port toggle
in/out on port 0x61 is the speaker-gate mechanism used to produce the tone -- October's observation, folded in as the second piece of evidence for the same name
0x03DB9: reads the next byte of the tune through tune_read_a
0x03DD5: XOR bit 1 of port 0x61. Ten callers, and the whole of the sound hardware
0x03DDE: tune_flags and sound_channel decide whether speaker_toggle fires this pass
0x03E16: swaps the words at DS:0xB87A and DS:0xB89C, copies DS:0xB89E to DS:0xB87C and moves the four at 0xB8A0..0xB8A6 down one place (image 0x3E16..0x3E42), seven words in all -- entries of the glyph-pointer table that draw_text indexes by letter through [bx - 0x4796] = DS:0xB86A

then clears bit 0 (and al, 0xfe) of nine bytes of each of twelve glyphs, bx = 2..0x22 skipping 4-8, 0xC and 0x1C; no port I/O; its one caller is startup at image 0x281, before the first card is drawn. Renamed 2026-11 from 'tune_next_note', which was named for its neighbours, not its body
0x03E7C: reads [si] until a 0; sub bl, 0x61 makes a letter an index, anything below 'a' only steps di by 2; a letter's glyph pointer comes through [bx - 0x4796] and its rows are ORed into [di] and [di + 2] with add di, 0x50 per row -- one 80-byte scanline; no port I/O

every caller loads SI with a string and DI with a screen position first (card_the_end: lea di, [0x20b6] / lea si, [0xdeb6]; title_animation: DI = the shadow at DS:0x337); the five title cards it draws matched the game's own frame 16000 of 16000 bytes (specification cycle 13). Renamed 2026-11 from 'sfx_step'
0x03F29: shifts DX:AX right by 2 x byte [0xDBB1] bits (shl cl, 1 / shr dx, 1 / rcr ax, 1) and returns at once when that byte is 0 -- a CGA pixel is two bits, so this moves a glyph row right by that many pixels

its one caller is draw_text at image 0x3ECD, between widening a glyph byte to two bits a pixel and ORing it into the frame; draw_text zeroes that byte on entry and after each letter adds the letter's advance and masks it with 3 -- the pixel phase within a byte. Renamed 2026-11 from 'sfx_clear'
0x03F71: 'and so this adventure ends', and the one card that waits for a key rather than a timer
0x03FFD: 'MAKE SURE YOUR KARATEKA', 'DISK IS IN DRIVE A', 'PRESS ANY KEY TO CONTINUE'
0x04028: draws the next line of text into the shadow at DS:0x337 with draw_text, then scrolls the CGA segment (ES=0xb800) up and feeds that line in a scanline at a time -- an animation, not a one-shot draw
calls read_intent inside the loop and returns immediately if a key was pressed -- an interruptible animation, consistent with the title screen
0x4149: dispatches on the returned key value (0x1b Esc, 0x12 sound-off, 0x13 sound-cycle, 0x16 ...) rather than issuing any DOS call itself
calls check_quit_key and intent_from_input and interprets their results -- a translation layer over lower-level input routines, matching 'read_intent' rather than a raw service
0x041FC: AH=7, INT 21h (direct console input, no echo) called twice in the body -- the literal 'poll' the name describes
remaps specific scancodes (0x4b/0x4d, arrow keys) to fixed values (0x34/0x36) before returning -- an input-remapping poll, not a passthrough
0x04233: calls check_quit_key until the buffer is empty, then clears input_latch
0x04241: pushes sound_on, sets it to 0 -- which is 'all sounds', not off -- calls play_sound(5) and pops sound_on back (image 0x4241..0x4256): sound 5 plays whatever mode the player chose

every caller is a settings key that has just been taken: Ctrl-R, Ctrl-S and Ctrl-V in read_intent (image 0x417F, 0x4190, 0x41B2) and j and k in handle_key (0x1DFD, 0x1E14). Renamed 2026-11 from 'stop_sound', which read the 0 as 'speaker off'
0x04257: a bare `ret`, followed by six bytes -- `mov ah, 0x0E / int 0x21 / ret` -- that nothing reaches
0x425E: port 0x3BA with a counted loop -- display detection, NOT the joystick
0x4273: writes a known pattern (0x55AA) then reads it back and checks for a match (jcxz) -- the detection test itself
on a match, builds a row-offset table using the 0x2000 CGA bank-interleave constant -- confirms the adapter really is CGA by setting up CGA-specific addressing
0x42D1: port 0x3BF, then the sync wait above
0x0433E: twelve CRTC registers out to port 0x3B4, which is the Hercules address
0x04352: calls detect_cga then, only if that fails, detect_hercules -- a genuine either/or choice between two adapters
returns a letter code (add al,0x41) distinguishing which adapter was chosen, consumed by callers as the result of the choice
0x04373: AL is loaded from the video_mode global set earlier by choose_adapter, not a fixed constant -- applies a previously-chosen mode, not merely 'a' mode
also writes the equipment_word byte into the BIOS data area (ds=0x40,si=0x10) before the mode change -- restoring BIOS state consistent with 'apply', not just 'set'
0x43AA: attacker's pose, distance and the target's stance in; 4 for a miss, 2 or 3 for a hit
rounds distance to a multiple of 4 and looks up reach (0xE0F8) and class (0xE112) tables before testing a 17-px band
0x4441: installs a vector, reads stick and keyboard, keeps input_mask
0x44D3: turns the stick bitmask into an intent, given the player's pose
0x04619: the four bounds, through calibrate_axis, with stick_present set if any of it answered
0x46FC: AH selects the axis, DI the pair of bounds to fill; called twice
0x4756: buttons plus both axes against the calibration bounds
0x047EE: four timings of one axis, averaged, subtracted from 0x310
0x04806: counts down from 0x310 while the axis bit stays high -- the paddle discharge
0x0482B: mov ax, 0x2524 / int 0x21 with DS set to the program's load segment (a relocation at image 0x482D) -- DOS AH=0x25 'Set Interrupt Vector' for vector 0x24
vector 0x24 is INT 24h, the DOS critical-error handler invoked on a disk error; the routine installs the program's own handler code rather than loading a table
0x483C: walks the FILE table (0xE1B0..0xE2C8, stride 14) looking for a free slot
the C standard-library open; compile_script calls it to open each script file before fgets reads a line
0x4883: seen opening with (name, 'r' at DS:0xBC83, FILE) -- the body fopen calls once a slot is free
hands the opened FILE slot back so the caller can fgets/fread from it
0x4A37: tests bit 1 of the FILE flag byte at [si+8] before flushing
compile_script calls it after the compile loop to flush the just-written output
0x4A91: the only unnamed routine that touches the FILE table fopen walks
flushes the FILE's buffered output, pairing with the putc/fwrite write path
0x4B0A: (buffer, 80, FILE); 2,602 calls from compile_script -- one per script line
reads up to 80 bytes (the script line length) and NUL-terminates, matching the C contract
0x4B7F: loops 0..19 at stride 14 -- every slot of the FILE table
closes each open slot at program end, the stdio shutdown pass
0x4BCE: reads the 32-bit break at [0x65]:[0x67] and asks DOS for more memory
moves the break pointer up when the allocator runs short
0x4C73: the same contract as heap_extend but growing upward; linked yet never called
a second allocator path the program ships but never exercises
0x4C99: checks the DOS version at [0x0F], then sets the break from [0x5D] and [0x61]
the one-time setup that establishes the heap bounds before any allocation
0x4D77: (handle) -> the same buffer address every time
the accessor every stdio read/write goes through to reach the FILE's buffer
0x4DB9: handed a filename, returns handle 3; the layer under fopen_body
turns a name into a DOS handle so the buffered layer above can read it
0x4FB8: or 0x301 into the mode word, mask 0x8000 off the handle
translates a C open mode string into the DOS access-mode bits
0x4FDD: (handle 3, ...); 136 calls from load_backdrop, show_castle and load_sprite_set, ~1,133 writes each
reads a requested byte count into the caller's buffer, the bulk-file read path
0x52D8: the mirror of fread: takes a handle, calls stdio_getbuf
writes bytes through the FILE buffer, the counterpart to the read path
0x5501: the shared error exit used when a caller passes an invalid argument
0x55F9: validates a file handle before the read/write/seek layer uses it
0x5659: the body of remove that actually deletes the file via DOS
0x5692: the C standard-library delete-file entry point
0x56A5: version check, then two path arguments
the C standard-library rename, passing old and new names to DOS
0x56DE: copies until NUL, n ignored; called with strcat from load_sprite_set to build 'ks0'+'.dat'
the C standard-library string-copy that appends a NUL terminator
0x5706: copies until NUL but no further than n, and NUL-terminates; not quite strncpy (which pads to n)
nothing calls it -- a library routine shipped but unused
0x5741: each compile_ arm calls it to parse the numbers out of a script command line
0x5879: that callback: 16,496 calls, one per character scanned
the character source sscanf pulls from, fed back one byte at a time
0x589A: walks a string one byte at a time; startup calls it
splits input into tokens for the command-line and config parsing
0x5907: the same shape, called once from crt0_main
parses the DOS command line into argc/argv for the C runtime
0x5953: the runtime's entry wrapper; called from the entry stub at 0x1F5
sets up stdin/stdout and calls main, the C runtime's start-up handoff
0x5B2E: respects n and stops at NUL; called from compile_line to match the command names
compares a script command against the 14 known verbs, bounded by length
0x5B9C: the four call sites pair with strcpy's, one per name built
appends the extension to a sprite-set stem to form the filename
0x5BCE: calls strlen and adds the result to the pointer
returns a pointer to the end of a string, used before appending
0x5C12: AH=0x4A before INT 21h is the DOS set-block-size call, not a generic service
BX is computed as a new paragraph count from block_paras/psp_segment before the call -- a resize, matching 'setblock'
0x5C57: AH=0x4A again, but with an additive size check (test ax,0xf000) guarding against overflow first
a second, related wrapper with its own stack frame and a different size computation
0x5C9B: AH=0x3C, DX=bp+4 (filename), CX=bp+6 (attributes) before INT 21h -- the exact Create File calling convention
jae branch stores the error code into dos_status only on failure -- a thin, direct wrapper
0x5CB5: AH=0x3D, DX=bp+4 (filename), AL=bp+6 (access mode) before INT 21h -- the exact Open File calling convention
same error-to-dos_status pattern as the other dos_* wrappers, confirming it belongs to the same family
0x5CCF: AH=0x3E, BX=bp+4 (handle) before INT 21h -- the exact Close File calling convention
single-argument wrapper, the simplest of the dos_* family, consistent with close needing only a handle
0x5CE6: AH=0x3F, BX=handle, CX=count(bp+8), DX=buffer(bp+6) before INT 21h -- the exact Read File calling convention
on error, zeroes AX in addition to storing dos_status -- a read-count-of-zero on failure, matching stdio-style read semantics
0x5D05: AH=0x40, with the identical BX/CX/DX argument layout as dos_read -- the write counterpart of the same family
0x5D24: AH=0x42, AL=bp+0xa (whence), BX=handle, CX:DX=offset -- the exact Move File Pointer calling convention
returns AX:DX recombined as BX:AX after the call -- the 32-bit new-position result lseek returns
0x5D48: AH=0x41, DX=bp+4 (filename) before INT 21h -- the exact Delete File calling convention
single-argument wrapper matching delete's one required parameter
0x5D5F: AH=0x43, AL=bp+6 (get/set flag), CX=bp+8 (attribute bits) before INT 21h -- the exact Get/Set Attribute convention
returns CX unmodified into AX after the call -- the attribute-get form of the same function
0x5D7E: AX=0x4400 -- AH=0x44 (IOCTL) with subfunction 0 (get device info), a specific IOCTL call, not a generic one
result (DX) is moved straight into AX for the caller -- a thin single-purpose wrapper
0x5D8D: AH=0x56, DX=bp+4 (old name), DI=bp+6 (new name) before INT 21h -- the exact Rename File two-name calling convention
two-pointer argument layout, distinct from every other single-name dos_* wrapper here
0x5DAB: hands two words to 0x023C, the runtime's terminator
0x5DBB: bdos(AH=0x08), console input without echo; confirmed as Lattice C 2.12's _CGET
reads one key without echo, the C runtime's unbuffered get-character
0x5DCF: bdos(AH=0x01), console input with echo; confirmed as Lattice C 2.12's _CGETE
reads one key and echoes it, the echoing variant of getch
0x5DE3: bdos(AH=0x02), console output; confirmed as Lattice C 2.12's _CPUT
writes one character to the console, the runtime's put-character
0x5DF7: bdos(AH=0x03), auxiliary input; confirmed as Lattice C 2.12's _AGET
reads one byte from the auxiliary (COM) port
0x5E0B: bdos(AH=0x04), auxiliary output; confirmed as Lattice C 2.12's _APUT
writes one byte to the auxiliary port
0x5E1F: bdos(AH=0x05), printer output; confirmed as Lattice C 2.12's _LPUT
writes one byte to the printer device
0x5E33: sscanf's engine; its second argument is 0x5879, a character-source callback
the scanf state machine that turns format specifiers into parsed values
0x6342: drains a FILE's buffer to its destination, the standard flush operation
0x644E: tests bits 4 and 5 of the FILE flag byte; recursive; the write engine
writes one byte through the FILE buffer, flushing when full

That sentence used to say 120 routine prologues, which was true and was
the wrong denominator. Lattice C's runtime is hand-written assembly with
no `push bp` at all, and neither are the tail entry points the compiler
generates inside a function -- so 56 routines the program calls had no
name while the count read 100%. The same mistake as quoting a reference
count for a data segment: a percentage needs its denominator said out
loud, and the denominator has to be the thing you care about.
The names are not equally strong. Each `why` says what it rests on -- a
probe four cases agreed on, an argument watched under emulation, a string
the routine draws, or the set of already-named variables it touches.
_globals_note: 199 of the 312 data-segment addresses the code names are named above --
64% of them, and 89% of every reference, because what is left is thin.
113 remain and 94 are referenced twice or fewer. Two uses give two data
points and no shape: not enough to tell a flag from a counter, let alone
what it counts. Naming them would produce names the next reader believes,
which this project has had to undo three times already.
The single finding that moved this most was not a naming technique at all.

_confirmed_by_library: Lattice C 2.12 for DOS (1984) was fetched and scanned against this image
with libscan.py. It matched 3 modules of 625 -- 0.2% -- and that number
understates what it settled: the three carry seven symbols, and all seven
land on addresses already named here from behaviour alone. Seven for seven.
The 0.2% is explained, not disappointing. Karateka names Lattice C **2.1**
and the obtainable release is **2.12**; the library was rebuilt between
those point releases, so most modules differ by a byte or two and an
exact-bytes scan refuses them -- correctly. The three that matched are the
small ones nobody had reason to change.
The memory model is **D**, not S: LCS.LIB matched nothing and LCD.LIB
matched all three. That agrees with the entry stub setting DS once to a
segment of its own while code is addressed from zero.

claimed 52 gaps of about 320 bytes; the real figure was 29 gaps of 7,944,
and the 99.5% quoted elsewhere came from a different measurement that
added string runs and variable widths on top of these spans rather than
from the spans themselves. Both are fixed.
